prompt.context: Euro Logistics is a large logistic company (similar in scale to Maersk). It provides logistics services only in Europe, operating many trucks, sea port terminals across Europe, and cargo ships. The logistics market is very competitive, and Euro Logistics believes that offering better customer service is a good way to differentiate itself in this market.
prompt.question: Euro Logistics wants to improve its customer satisfaction index. What should they do?

clarifying_info.q: What types of assets and services does Euro Logistics operate?
clarifying_info.a: They have many trucks, sea port terminals all around Europe, and cargo ships.

clarifying_info.q: Why is Euro Logistics focused on customer satisfaction rather than cost or pricing?
clarifying_info.a: The logistics market is very competitive, and Euro Logistics understands that offering better customer service is a good way to differentiate themselves in this market.

clarifying_info.q: Do we have data on how customers currently evaluate Euro Logistics' service?

exhibits.title: Customer Satisfaction Survey
exhibits.shows: Horizontal bar charts for 9 European countries (Germany, England, Norway, Sweden, Italy, Netherlands, Ireland, Scotland, France), each showing the top 3 most important service dimensions ranked by importance and their satisfaction scores. Scores above 75 are considered good. Dimensions include Delivery Time, Billing, Customer Service, and Order Tracking.

framework: Map the full customer value chain: pre-shipment (order placement, billing), in-transit (tracking, communication), and post-delivery (billing resolution, customer service follow-up)
Assess current performance on each dimension using customer satisfaction data by country
Identify dimensions with lowest scores AND highest importance across countries
Prioritize improvements by impact (score gap vs. threshold of 75) and feasibility
Quantify the financial return of investments in underperforming areas (churn reduction, payback period)
Develop implementation roadmap for quick wins vs. longer-term system upgrades

questions.prompt: What can you conclude from the Customer Satisfaction Survey (Exhibit 1)? Is there a particular measure or country that Euro Logistics should pay special attention to?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should: (1) note that scores above 75 are good and identify which dimensions fall below that threshold; (2) observe that Billing and Order Tracking consistently appear as important dimensions across many countries and have the lowest average scores; (3) note that Customer Service is highly rated and important; (4) recognize that Delivery Time has some low scores but delays are caused by customs — the only actionable improvement is providing more realistic delivery deadlines. Candidate should recommend focusing on Billing and Order Tracking systems. Ireland stands out as having all three scores below 75 (65, 67, 73).

questions.prompt: Euro Logistics wants to improve its Billing and Order Tracking systems. The investment will cost 5 M Euros per system (10 M total). The new systems are estimated to reduce the churn rate by 20%. Should they invest? What is the payback period?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate revenues lost to churn, then savings from reduced churn, then divide total investment by annual savings. Should compare payback period against the 2-year goal and recommend investing if payback is under 2 years. Key insight: use revenues lost (not net margin) because avoided churn preserves the full revenue stream.

math.setup: Revenue lost per year = Total Revenue x Churn Rate. Savings = Revenue lost x Churn reduction %. Payback = Total Investment / Annual Savings.
steps: Revenue lost per year = 150 M x 25% = 37.5 M euros
Savings from new systems = 37.5 M x 20% = 7.5 M euros
Total investment = 5 M + 5 M = 10 M euros
Payback period = 10 M / 7.5 M = 1.33 years = approximately 1 year and 4 months
math.answer: Payback period is approximately 1 year and 4 months, which is under the 2-year goal. Euro Logistics should invest.

recommendation: Euro Logistics should invest 10 M euros to upgrade its Billing and Order Tracking systems, which are the two dimensions with the lowest satisfaction scores and highest importance across European markets.
The investment pays back in approximately 1 year and 4 months — well within the 2-year goal — by reducing annual churn-driven revenue loss from 37.5 M to 30 M euros.
For Delivery Time, Euro Logistics cannot control customs delays but should set more realistic delivery deadlines to improve perceived reliability.
risks: The 20% churn reduction is an estimate; actual retention gains may be lower if other factors drive churn.
System implementation may take time, delaying the payback timeline beyond projections.
Ireland and England have multiple dimensions below 75; broader service improvements beyond Billing and Tracking may be needed in those markets.
next_steps: Conduct RFP for Billing and Order Tracking system vendors; evaluate build vs. buy options.
Pilot new systems in one or two markets before full European rollout.
Establish baseline churn metrics and track post-implementation to validate the 20% improvement assumption.
Review Delivery Time SLAs by lane to set more accurate customer expectations around customs delays.
